historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable: buybacks drove stockholders' equity negative in FY2022 (-5,768) and it has since been rebuilt by retained earnings and ~25bn of new equity (FY2021 5,952 to FY2026 43,056, a meaningless 48.6%/yr; FY2023 base of 1,556 gives no sensible 3-year figure). It diverges from revenue and EPS by far more than 30%, so revenue growth is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, net debtor): FY2021 11,249; FY2023 3,720; FY2024 5,793; FY2025 -5,968; FY2026 -28,608. No CAGR is defined on a series that ends negative. The collapse is capex (2,135 in FY2021 to 55,663 in FY2026), not operations: OCF doubled over the same period. FY2026 EPS of 5.83 includes a 2.7bn gain on the Ampere sale, which flatters the 3-year EPS CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: The 664bn of remaining performance obligations converts, but late and not in full. The 10-Q schedules 13% (~86bn) for the next twelve months and 37% (~123bn a year) for months 13-36; base revenue of ~90bn in FY2027 (management guides to at least 90bn; Q1 was 19.3bn, +30%, with cloud infrastructure +121%, and Q2 is guided to +30-34%), ~120bn in FY2028 and ~146bn in FY2029 runs roughly 10-15% under that schedule once non-backlog revenue is added, and total revenue reaches ~225bn only in FY2036. Capital expenditure is ~112bn in FY2027 (Q1 alone was 28.5bn and management says FY2027 exceeds FY2026's 55.7bn) and ~95bn in FY2028, then falls toward a replacement level of ~26-27% of revenue; cumulative owner FCF is about -100bn over FY2027-FY2029, so net debt roughly doubles before FCF turns positive in FY2030. EBITDA margin rises from ~54% (FY2026, pre-SBC, ex-restructuring; 58% in Q1 FY2027) to 60% because rented GPU capacity is depreciation-heavy rather than opex-heavy, but depreciation climbs from 14% to 29% of revenue, so the owner EBIT margin dips to the mid-20s before recovering to ~30%. Mature owner-FCF margin is ~24%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Every large AI contract performs on schedule and Oracle finds the power, sites, chips and financing to deliver it: revenue ~132bn in FY2028 and ~217bn in FY2030, in line with the backlog timing, then ~315bn by FY2036 as renewals and follow-on demand keep the fleet full. Capex peaks higher (~125bn in FY2028) and the funding gap is wider, but utilisation is high, AI gross margins settle at the top of the 30-40% range, EBITDA margin reaches 62% and the multicloud database and SaaS businesses keep growing underneath. Requires several independent things to go right: customer solvency, power availability, GPU supply, and debt markets staying open at investment-grade spreads.
scenario_narratives.bear: Oracle's own risk factor is the bear case: OCI is concentrated among a small number of large, in some cases highly leveraged, customers, and if they fail to perform Oracle is left with multi-year data-centre leases (288bn not yet commenced, 15-19 year terms, longer than the customer contracts) and related financings without the revenue. Revenue still grows to ~88bn in FY2027, just short of guidance, on capacity already contracted and built, then stalls at ~110-128bn as contracts are renegotiated, deferred or defaulted. FY2027 capex is largely committed (~100bn) before it can be cut. Stranded capacity and lease cost pull EBITDA margin down to 51-52% while depreciation on the installed fleet runs at 25-29% of revenue for years. Net debt peaks above 180bn against ~55bn of EBITDA; with S&P already at BBB-, a fall to high yield or a dilutive equity raise at depressed prices is likely on this path and is not captured in the per-share value, so the bear figure should be read as an upper bound for that state of the world.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Oracle is valued as two businesses in one set of flows: a mature, high-margin software and support franchise (~49bn of revenue) and a rapidly scaling, capital-intensive AI infrastructure lessor whose 664bn backlog has to be built before it can be billed. Value is almost entirely in the terminal years; the explicit period is a funding gap. The question the model answers is not whether the backlog is large but what it is worth after the ~2.5-3 dollars of capex each dollar of annual infrastructure revenue requires, the fleet's replacement cost, and the debt taken on to build it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Counterparty concentration: a small number of AI customers account for most of the backlog; no single customer was 10% of FY2026 revenue yet, so the dependency lies ahead, not behind
Funding: base-case cumulative owner FCF of roughly -100bn over FY2027-FY2029 on top of ~117bn of net debt-like claims; further equity issuance is not modelled
Lease mismatch: 288bn of uncommenced data-centre leases with 15-19 year terms against shorter customer contracts
Replacement capex: terminal capex of ~27% of revenue assumes a blended asset life near 7-8 years; a 5-year GPU life would cut mature FCF margin by several points

Terminal value is ~83% of base enterprise value and the first three years are cash-negative, so value is very sensitive to the discount rate (base value per share falls by roughly a quarter for each point of required return) and to the mature margin
Unverified inputs: the capex-financing balance (~3.9bn) and the NCI market value (~4bn) are estimates

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 109.21-250.25
data_sources.financials: ORCL_Metrics.csv / ORCL.duckdb; FY2026 Form 10-K (year ended 31 May 2026); Q1 FY2027 Form 10-Q (quarter ended 31 Aug 2026) for the balance sheet, share count, leases, RPO schedule and ATM issuance
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 10-K risk factors and MD&A, Q1 FY2027 10-Q MD&A; ORCL_Analysis.json (guidance: FY2027 revenue of at least 90bn, capex above FY2026; S&P BBB-; roughly half of RPO attributed to OpenAI by analyst estimates)

inputs.share_count_basis: 3,024m common outstanding at 31 Aug 2026 (10-Q balance sheet; 3,023.7m on the cover at 7 Sep 2026) + 34m treasury-method dilution from employee plans (Q1 FY2027 EPS note) + 31.2m from the 6.50% Series D Mandatory Convertible Preferred at its MAXIMUM conversion rate (50,000 preferred shares x 624.7657; the maximum applies below roughly $160/share and the stock is well under that). Held FLAT thereafter because SBC is expensed in the flows. The 141m shares sold through the $20bn at-the-market program in Q1 FY2027 are genuine non-SBC issuance and are already in the count; any further equity raise to fund the buildout is NOT modelled and would be dilutive at prices below intrinsic value.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Debt-like claims at 31 Aug 2026: notes payable and other borrowings 125,337 (7,625 current + 117,712 non-current) + finance lease liabilities 9,185 + short-term financing related to capital expenditures ~3,937 (net proceeds 1,422 FY25 + 3,345 FY26 - 830 Q1 FY27; estimate, balance not separately disclosed) + customer prepayments with a significant financing component 15,955 (4,592 FY26 + 11,363 Q1 FY27: cash already received and sitting in the cash balance for revenue the projections count again as it is recognised, so it is a debt-equivalent). Less cash and marketable securities 37,077. Operating lease liabilities (34,621) are EXCLUDED because operating lease cost is charged inside EBITDA. Not deducted: 12,060 of non-current income taxes payable and 6,247 of unpaid capital expenditures.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was 780 but Oracle is a large net debtor, so nothing is stripped; the component build starts from operating EBITDA and carries no interest income in any case.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K: stock-based compensation 4,811 (1,618 operating segments + 3,193 R&D and G&A; cash-flow add-back) plus 111 of shares repurchased for tax withholdings on vesting. Oracle publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Cost of equity ~10.8% (US 10-year ~4.3% + 5% ERP x beta ~1.3, the beta reflecting the leverage and customer concentration now attached to the equity); after-tax cost of debt ~4.5-5% (S&P cut the issuer rating to BBB- in July 2026); roughly 74/26 equity/debt at market values gives ~9.2%, rounded to 9.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: the financing and counterparty risk is carried by the scenario paths and the bear weight, not by a second premium in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases stay in the flows: US GAAP operating lease cost (2,794 in FY2026, ~3,800 annualised on Q1 FY2027 cash paid) is an operating expense inside EBITDA, and the EBITDA margin paths absorb the step-up as the 288,000 of not-yet-commenced data-centre leases (15-19 year terms, commencing Q2 FY2027 to FY2029) come on. Operating lease liabilities are therefore not in net debt. Finance leases (9,185) are in net debt because their cost sits in depreciation and interest, outside EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; noncontrolling interests (Oracle Financial Services Software, Oracle Corporation Japan) deducted once in the equity bridge at ~18x their FY2026 share of income (222), since book NCI of 424 badly understates two listed subsidiaries.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (FY2027-FY2036). Oracle is an operating company (cloud, software, hardware, services), so the owner-FCF row of the dcf-methods routing table applies; the 10-year horizon is needed because FCF is deeply negative through the AI data-centre buildout and does not mature until about FY2032. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF and no memory entry. Scenario axes come from the FY2026 10-K, the Q1 FY2027 10-Q and the Analysis JSON (FY2027 revenue guided to at least 90bn; no long-term FCF inflection guided). Price is a regular Friday close, not an after-hours print. Reported FCF is NEGATIVE (FY2026 OCF 31,977 - capex 55,663 = -23,686; Q1 FY2027 capex alone 28,499) and Q1 FY2027 OCF of 23,103 includes 11,363 of customer prepayments that are financing in substance. Buybacks have effectively stopped (93 in FY2026) and Oracle is now a net ISSUER of equity (19,909 ATM in Q1 FY2027, 4,954 mandatory convertible preferred in FY2026), so the flat share count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding. The restructuring charge (1,838 in FY2026) is treated as largely non-recurring in the margin paths. Finance-lease ROU additions (1,539 in Q1 FY2027) are non-cash and sit outside reported capex; the capex paths are set with that in mind. Data caveat: the Metrics CSV total_debt column carries only the current portion of borrowings (7,199 at FY2026) and is not usable; debt here is read off the 10-Q balance sheet.

bear.narrative: Large AI customers renegotiate or default: revenue stalls near 110-128bn with capacity and leases already committed.

base.narrative: Backlog converts with slippage: revenue ~90bn FY2027 (the guided floor), ~120bn FY2028, ~167bn FY2030, ~225bn only by FY2036.

bull.narrative: Backlog converts on the contracted schedule: revenue ~132bn FY2028, ~217bn FY2030, ~315bn FY2036.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 30% because the thesis rests on a concentrated set of AI counterparties whose ability to pay is unproven, funded by a balance sheet that has added ~43bn of notes, a 5bn convertible and a 20bn at-the-market equity sale in five quarters. Base stays at 50%: the backlog is contractual and FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 revenue tracked it. Bull cut to 20% because it needs customer solvency, power and chip supply, and open debt markets to all hold at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
